q: 1. The mass per unit volume of a liquid at a standard temperature and pressure is called
explain: Mass density (ρ) is defined as the mass of a substance per unit volume. In contrast, specific weight is weight per unit volume.

q: 2. The weight per unit volume of a liquid at a standard temperature and pressure is called
explain: Specific weight (w or γ) represents the force exerted by gravity on a unit volume of a fluid.

q: 3. The specific weight of water in S.I. units is taken as
explain: All these values are equivalent: 9.81 kN/m³ = 9810 N/m³. Converting to mm³, it becomes 9.81 x 10⁻⁶ N/mm³.

q: 4. The ratio of specific weight of a liquid to the specific weight of pure water at a standard temperature is called
explain: Specific gravity (S) is a dimensionless ratio comparing a liquid's density or specific weight to that of a standard fluid (water at 4°C).

q: 5. The specific gravity of water is taken as
explain: Water is the standard reference for liquids, so its specific gravity is defined as 1.

q: 6. The specific weight of sea water is _________ that of pure water
explain: Sea water contains dissolved salts, making it denser and heavier per unit volume than pure water.

q: 7. The mass of 2.5 m³ of a certain liquid is 2 tonnes. Its mass density is
explain: Density = Mass / Volume. 2 tonnes = 2000 kg. So, 2000 / 2.5 = 800 kg/m³.

q: 8. The specific gravity of an oil whose specific weight is 7.85 kN/m³, is
explain: Specific Gravity = Specific weight of oil / Specific weight of water = 7.85 / 9.81 ≈ 0.8.

q: 9. A vessel of 4 m³ contains an oil which weights 30 kN. The specific weight of the oil is
explain: Specific weight = Total Weight / Total Volume = 30 kN / 4 m³ = 7.5 kN/m³.

q: 10. The property of a liquid which offers resistance to the movement of one layer of liquid over another adjacent layer of liquid, is called
explain: Viscosity is the internal friction of a fluid that resists the relative motion of its layers.

q: 11. The force per unit length is the unit of
explain: Surface tension is defined as the force acting per unit length (N/m) along the surface of a liquid.

q: 12. The variation in the volume of a liquid with the variation of pressure is called
explain: Compressibility is the measure of the relative volume change of a fluid as a response to a pressure change.

q: 13. A glass tube of smaller diameter is used while performing an experiment for the capillary rise of water because
options: it is easier to see through the glass tube
glass tube is cheaper than a metallic tube
it is not possible to conduct this experiment with any other tube
explain: While small diameters increase the height of capillary rise (making it measurable), glass is used specifically for its transparency to allow for clear observation of the meniscus.

q: 14. The mercury does not wet the glass. This is due to the property of the liquid known as
explain: Mercury has higher cohesive forces (attraction between its own molecules) than adhesive forces (attraction to glass), causing it to avoid 'wetting' the surface.

q: 15. With an increase in size of tube, the rise or depression of liquid in the tube due to surface tension will
options: depend upon the characteristics of liquid
explain: Capillary rise (h) is inversely proportional to the diameter of the tube (d) according to the formula h = (4σ cosθ) / (ρgd).

q: 16. The unit of surface tension is
explain: As it represents the force acting along a line on the surface, its SI unit is Newtons per metre (N/m).

q: 17. Falling drops of water become spheres due to the property of
explain: Surface tension acts to minimize the surface area of a liquid volume; a sphere has the minimum surface area for a given volume.

q: 18. The intensity of pressure at point, in a liquid, is
options: directly proportional to the area of the vessel containing liquid
directly proportional to the depth of liquid from the surface
directly proportional to the length of the vessel containing liquid
inversely proportional to the depth of liquid from the surface
explain: According to hydrostatic law, P = ρgh, meaning pressure increases linearly with depth (h).

q: 19. The pressure intensity in kN/m² (or kPa) at any point in a liquid is
explain: Pressure (P) is the product of specific weight (w) and depth (h).

q: 20. The pressure at a point 4 m below the free surface of water is
explain: P = wh = 9.81 kN/m³ * 4 m = 39.24 kN/m² (kPa).

q: 21. The height of a water column equivalent to a pressure of 0.15 MPa is
explain: h = P / w. Converting 0.15 MPa to 150 kPa: 150 / 9.81 ≈ 15.3 m.

q: 22. When the pressure intensity at point is more than the local atmospheric pressure, then the difference of these two pressure is called
explain: Gauge pressure is measured relative to atmospheric pressure. If it is higher, it is specifically called positive gauge pressure.

q: 23. The absolute pressure is equal to
explain: Absolute pressure is the total pressure measured from a perfect vacuum (zero reference).

q: 24. The pressure less than atmospheric pressure is known as
explain: All these terms describe pressures below the local atmospheric level.

q: 25. The pressure of a liquid measured with the help of a piezometer tube is
explain: A piezometer measures the pressure head relative to the atmosphere, thus providing gauge pressure.

q: 26. The pressure measured with the help of a piezometer tube is in
explain: A piezometer measures pressure by the vertical height (h) to which the liquid rises in the tube.

q: 27. A piezometer tube is used only for measuring
explain: Piezometers are unsuitable for very high pressures (tube would be too long) or vacuum pressures (air would enter the tube).

q: 28. The liquid used in manometers should have
explain: High-density liquids (like mercury) allow for shorter manometer tubes when measuring high pressures.

q: 29. A manometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressures between two points in a pipe
explain: While differential manometers measure pressure differences, a standard manometer (like a U-tube) is used for point pressure in pipes/channels.

q: 30. A manometer is used to measure
explain: Manometers are generally employed for measuring higher pressures compared to simple piezometers.

q: 31. A differential manometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressures between two points in a pipe
explain: The specific purpose of a differential manometer is to determine the pressure head difference between two distinct points.

q: 32. The total pressure on a horizontally immersed surface is
explain: Total pressure (P) = specific weight (w) * Area (A) * depth of centroid (x̄).

q: 33. The total pressure on an immersed surface inclined at an angle θ with the liquid surface is
explain: Total pressure is independent of the angle of inclination and depends only on the area and the depth of the centroid.

q: 34. The point at which the resultant pressure on an immersed surface acts, is known as
explain: The Centre of Pressure is the point where the total hydrostatic force is considered to act.

q: 35. The depth of centre of pressure (h̄) for a vertically immersed surface from the liquid surface is given by
explain: This is the standard formula derived using the parallel axis theorem for pressure distribution.

q: 36. The centre of pressure for a vertically immersed surface lies at a distance equal to _________ the centre of gravity.
explain: The centre of pressure always lies below the centre of gravity because pressure increases with depth.

q: 37. The depth of centre of pressure for an immersed surface inclined at an angle θ with the liquid surface lies at a distance equal to _________ the centre of gravity.
explain: For inclined surfaces, the vertical distance below the centroid is adjusted by the sin² θ component.

q: 38. A vertical wall is subjected to a pressure due to one kind of liquid, on one of its sides. The total pressure on the wall per unit length is
explain: P = w * Area * x̄. For unit length (1m) and depth H, Area = H * 1 and x̄ = H/2. Thus, P = wH²/2.

q: 39. A water tank contains 1.3 m deep water. The pressure exerted by the water per metre length of the tank is
40. A vertical wall is subjected to a pressure due to one kind of liquid, on one of its sides. The total pressure on the wall acts at a distance _________ from the liquid surface.
explain: The centre of pressure for a rectangular vertical surface is at 2/3 of the depth from the top (free surface).

q: 41. When a vertical wall is subjected to pressures due to liquid on both sides, the resultant pressure is the _________ of the two pressures.
explain: Forces act in opposite directions, so the net force is the difference between the pressures on each side.

q: 42. In a lockgate, the reaction between two gates is
explain: The reaction R at the hinge/meeting point is calculated as P / (2 sin α) based on force equilibrium.

q: 43. The water pressure per metre length on a vertical masonary wall of dam is
explain: This follows the same logic as Q.38 for the total hydrostatic force on a vertical surface.

q: 44. When a body is placed over a liquid, it will sink down if
options: gravitational force is equal to the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is less than the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is more than the upthrust of the liquid
explain: If the downward weight exceeds the upward buoyant force, the body will have a net downward acceleration.

q: 45. When a body is placed over a liquid, it will float if
options: gravitational force is equal to the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is less than the upthrust of the liquid
gravitational force is more than the upthrust of the liquid
explain: A body floats when its weight is less than or equal to the maximum possible upthrust (weight of the fully displaced volume).

q: 46. When a body is immersed wholly or partially in a liquid, it is lifted up by a force equal to weight of liquid displaced by the body. This statement is called
explain: This is the fundamental definition of Archimedes' Principle regarding buoyancy.

q: 47. The centre of gravity of the volume of the liquid displaced is called
explain: The buoyant force acts through the centroid of the displaced volume, known as the Centre of Buoyancy.

q: 48. The buoyancy depends upon the
options: pressure with which the liquid is displaced
explain: According to Archimedes' Principle, the magnitude of the buoyant force is exactly equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.

q: 49. A uniform body 3 m long, 2 m wide and 1 m deep floats in water. If the depth of immersion is 0.6 m, then the weight of the body is
explain: Weight = Displaced volume * w = (3 * 2 * 0.6) * 9.81 = 3.6 * 9.81 ≈ 35.3 kN.

q: 50. When a body, floating in a liquid, is given a small angular displacement, it starts oscillating about a point known as
explain: The Metacentre is the point of intersection of the vertical through the new centre of buoyancy and the original axis of the body.

q: 51. The metacentric heights of two floating bodies A and B are 1 m and 1.5 m respectively. Select the correct statement
options: The bodies A and B have equal stability
The body A is more stable than body B
The body B is more stable than body A
The bodies A and B are unstable
explain: Stability of a floating body is directly proportional to its metacentric height (GM). A higher GM provides a larger restoring couple.

q: 52. If a body floating in a liquid returns back to its original position, when given a small angular displacement, the body is said to be in
explain: Stable equilibrium occurs when the metacentre (M) is above the centre of gravity (G), creating a restoring moment.

q: 53. A body floating in a liquid is said to be in neutral equilibrium, if its metacentre
options: coincides with its centre of gravity
lies above its centre of gravity
lies below its centre of gravity
lies between the centre of buoyancy and centre of gravity
explain: In neutral equilibrium, M and G coincide, meaning no restoring or overturning moment is produced when the body is tilted.

q: 54. The time of oscillation of a floating body is given by
explain: The time period (T) formula is T = 2π√(k² / (GM·g)), where k is the radius of gyration and h (or GM) is the metacentric height.

q: 55. The metacentric height of a ship is 0.6 m and the radius of gyration is 4 m. The time of rolling of ship is
56. One cubic metre of water weighs
explain: By standard metric definition, 1 cubic metre (m³) of volume is equivalent to 1000 litres of liquid.

q: 57. One litre of water occupies a volume of
explain: Since 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³ and 1 m³ = 1000 litres, then 1 litre = 1000 cm³.

q: 58. When a liquid is flowing through a pipe, the velocity of the liquid is
options: maximum at the centre and minimum near the walls
minimum at the centre and maximum near the walls
zero at the centre and maximum near the walls
maximum at the centre and zero near the walls
explain: Due to viscosity and the 'no-slip condition' at the boundaries, velocity is zero at the walls and reaches its peak at the pipe's centerline.

q: 59. The imaginary line drawn in the fluid in such a way that the tangent to any point gives the direction of motion at that point, is known as
explain: A streamline is a curve that is everywhere tangent to the local velocity vector of the fluid flow.

q: 60. The flow in a pipe or channel is said to be uniform when
options: the liquid particles at all sections have the same velocities
the liquid particles at different sections have different velocities
explain: Uniform flow is defined by velocity (and other flow parameters) remaining constant with respect to distance along the flow path.

q: 61. The flow in a pipe or channel is said to be non-uniform when
options: the liquid particles at all sections have the same velocities
the liquid particles at different sections have different velocities
the quantity of liquid flowing per second is constant
each liquid particle has a definite path
explain: Non-uniform flow occurs when the velocity changes from one cross-section to another at a given instant.

q: 62. A flow in which each liquid particle has a definite path, and the paths of individual particles do not cross each other, is called
explain: In streamline (laminar) flow, fluid layers slide over each other without mixing or crossing paths.

q: 63. A flow in which the quantity of liquid flowing per second is constant, is called _________ flow.
explain: Steady flow is defined as flow where properties (like discharge/velocity) do not change with respect to time.

q: 64. A flow in which the quantity of liquid flowing per second is not constant, is called
explain: Unsteady flow occurs when parameters at a point vary over time.

q: 65. According to equation of continuity
explain: For an incompressible fluid, the volume flow rate (Area * Velocity) must remain constant across different sections.

q: 66. A flow through a long pipe at constant rate is called
explain: Constant rate makes it steady; a long pipe of constant diameter makes it uniform.

q: 67. A flow through an expanding tube at constant rate is called
explain: It is steady (constant rate), but non-uniform because the expanding area causes velocity to change along the length.

q: 68. A flow whose streamline is represented by a curve, is called
explain: When flow velocity is a function of two space coordinates (e.g., x and y), the streamlines become curves in a plane.

q: 69. A flow whose streamline is represented by a straight line, is called _________ dimensional flow.
explain: In 1D flow, fluid parameters vary along a single direction, resulting in straight parallel streamlines.

q: 70. In one dimensional flow, the flow
explain: The key characteristic is that the flow parameters only change along the direction of flow, which is typically a straight line path.

q: 71. The total energy of a liquid particle in motion is equal to
options: pressure energy + kinetic energy + potential energy
explain: Based on Bernoulli's principle, total energy is the summation of these three forms of energy.

q: 72. The total head of a liquid particle in motion is equal to
options: pressure head + kinetic head + potential head
explain: Total head (H) = P/w + v²/2g + Z. It represents the energy per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 73. For a perfect incompressible liquid, flowing in a continuous stream, the total energy of a particle remains the same... This statement is called
explain: This is the core definition of Bernoulli's theorem for ideal fluid flow.

q: 74. According to Bernoulli's equation
explain: This represents the conservation of energy where potential, pressure, and kinetic heads sum to a constant value.

q: 75. Euler's equation in the differential form for the motion of liquids is given by
explain: Euler's equation relates pressure, gravity, and acceleration in a fluid, assuming no friction.

q: 76. Bernoulli's equation is applied to
explain: All three listed devices work by measuring pressure/velocity changes based on Bernoulli's principle.

q: 77. Barometer is used to measure
options: difference of pressure between two points in a pipe
explain: The barometer is specifically designed to measure local atmospheric pressure.

q: 78. Venturimeter is used to
options: measure the velocity of a flowing liquid
measure the pressure of a flowing liquid
measure the discharge of liquid flowing in a pipe
measure the pressure difference of liquid flowing between two points
explain: A venturimeter is a standard device used to calculate the volume flow rate (discharge) in a pipeline.

q: 79. The length of the divergent cone in a venturimeter is _________ that of the convergent cone.
explain: The divergent cone is longer (angle of 5-7°) to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss.

q: 80. The velocity of the liquid flowing through the divergent portion of a venturimeter
explain: As the cross-sectional area increases in the divergent part, the velocity must decrease per the continuity equation.

q: 81. The divergent portion of a venturimeter is made longer than convergent portion in order to
options: avoid the tendency of breaking away the stream of liquid
explain: A gradual expansion (longer length) ensures the flow stays attached to the walls, preventing turbulence and boundary layer separation.

q: 82. In order to measure the flow with a venturimeter, it is installed in
options: any direction and in any location
explain: A venturimeter works accurately in any orientation as long as the Bernoulli equation accounts for the change in elevation (Z).

q: 83. A pitot tube is used to measure the
options: velocity of flow at the required point in a pipe
pressure difference between two points in a pipe
total pressure of liquid flowing in a pipe
explain: The pitot tube measures stagnation pressure to determine the point velocity of the fluid.

q: 84. Coefficient of resistance is the ratio of
options: area at vena contracta to area of orifice
loss of head in the orifice to the head available at exit
explain: Coefficient of resistance (Cr) relates the energy loss due to friction to the available kinetic head.

q: 85. A jet of water discharging from a 40 mm diameter orifice has a diameter of 32 mm at its vena contracta. The coefficient of contraction is
explain: Cc = Area of jet / Area of orifice = (32/40)² = 0.8² = 0.64.

q: 86. Coefficient of velocity is defined as the ratio of
options: actual velocity of jet at vena contracta to the theoretical velocity
area of jet at vena contracta to the area of orifice
actual discharge through an orifice to the theoretical discharge
explain: Cv = Actual Velocity / Theoretical Velocity. It accounts for losses due to friction.

q: 87. The theoretical velocity of jet at vena contracta is
explain: Derived from Bernoulli's equation (v = √2gh), assuming no losses.

q: 88. Coefficient of discharge Cd is equal to
explain: The overall discharge coefficient is the product of the contraction and velocity coefficients.

q: 89. An average value of coefficient of velocity is
explain: For a standard sharp-edged orifice, Cv typically ranges from 0.95 to 0.99.

q: 90. The coefficient of velocity is determined experimentally by using the relation
explain: Using the trajectory of the jet, where x is horizontal distance and y is vertical drop, this formula solves for actual velocity.

q: 91. An orifice is said to be large, if
options: the size of orifice is large
the velocity of flow is large
the available head is more than 5 times the height of orifice
the available head is less than 5 times the height of orifice
explain: If head H < 5d, the pressure variation across the orifice is significant, and it is classified as a 'large orifice'.

q: 92. A pipe of length more than double the diameter of orifice fitted externally or internally to the orifice is called a
explain: A mouthpiece is a short tube used to increase the discharge through an orifice.

q: 93. In a short cylindrical external mouthpiece, the vena contracta occurs at a distance _________ the diameter of the orifice from the outlet of orifice.
explain: For an external mouthpiece, the jet contracts to its minimum area at approximately 0.25d from the inlet.

q: 94. The loss of head due to sudden enlargement is
explain: This loss represents energy dissipated through turbulence as flow transitions to a larger pipe.

q: 95. The loss of head due to sudden contraction, assuming coefficient of contraction as 0.62, is
explain: Based on (1/Cc - 1)² * (v₂²/2g). With Cc = 0.62, the factor is approx 0.375.

q: 96. The loss of head at entrance in a pipe is
explain: Standard minor loss coefficient for a sharp-edged entrance is K = 0.5.

q: 97. The loss of head at exit of a pipe is
explain: At the exit, the entire kinetic energy (v²/2g) is lost as the fluid enters the reservoir.

q: 98. The discharge through an external mouth piece is given by
explain: The average Cd for an external mouthpiece is 0.855, significantly higher than a simple orifice (0.62).

q: 99. The coefficient of discharge for an external mouthpiece depends upon
explain: The length relative to diameter determines whether the mouthpiece runs full, affecting the Cd.

q: 100. In an internal mouthpiece, if the jet after contraction does not touch the sides of the mouthpiece, then the mouthpiece is said to be
explain: When the jet discharges without wetting the internal walls, it is in a 'running free' condition.
